svg.aria-label: Fig 3. Planned appeal writer. Facts from a synthetic denial record and chunks of a fictional payer policy, ZZP01, go into the Muse writer, a Meta model that drafts the letter. A citation gate with two rollers checks that each statement cites a chunk ID; a statement with no source goes back to the writer on a red track. A human approves the letter in the review console, tier 2. The appeal goes to the send tray only after approval. Planned, not built.
svg.title: Fig 3. Planned appeal writer. Facts from a synthetic denial record and chunks of a fictional payer policy, ZZP01, go into the Muse writer, a Meta model that drafts the letter. A citation gate with two rollers checks that each statement cites a chunk ID; a statement with no source goes back to the writer on a red track. A human approves the letter in the review console, tier 2. The appeal goes to the send tray only after approval. Planned, not built.
svg.text: Fictional payer policy. Synthetic claim. Planned design, not built.
no citation, no letter · no approval, no send
1 Inputs: the synthetic denial record, the facts from the record, and retrieved chunks
of a fictional payer policy (example payer ZZP01).
2 Muse (a Meta model) drafts the letter. Muse writes the text. It does not make the decision.
3 The citation gate checks that each statement maps to a retrieved chunk ID.
If a statement has no source, the draft goes back to the writer (red track).
4 A human approves the letter in the review console (tier 2). In the hackathon,
5 The appeal goes out only after approval. Then the voice agent follows up.
